issues.description: audio_format derived by f-string from sample_rate without validating against the STTAudioFormat Literal
issues.detail: typing.cast(STTAudioFormat, f"pcm_{sample_rate}") silently produces invalid formats (e.g. pcm_11025, pcm_32000) for any sample_rate outside the Literal set. The cast lies to the type checker and the server rejects the connection at runtime with an opaque error. Validate sample_rate against the allowed set in __init__ and fail loudly.

issues.description: Query string built by hand-rolled f-strings instead of urlencode/aiohttp params
issues.detail: Query params are accumulated as a list of f-strings and joined with '&'. The first language_code or value with a reserved character will produce a malformed URL. Build a dict, drop None entries, and let urllib.parse.urlencode or aiohttp's params= serialize. Small fix, removes a class of escaping bugs and keeps options inspectable as data.

issues.description: Speaking-state machine duplicates START_OF_SPEECH dispatch and conflates two segment-end signals
issues.detail: The 'if not self._speaking: emit START_OF_SPEECH; self._speaking=True' block is copy-pasted across partial_transcript and committed_transcript handlers, and end-of-segment is overloaded onto an empty committed_transcript. Extract a pure transition function (or _mark_speaking helper) so the state machine lives in one place with a stated invariant, and model end-of-segment as its own event.

issues.description: tasks_group.exception() called on a cancelled gather in finally can mask real errors
issues.detail: After gracefully_cancel and tasks_group.cancel(), calling tasks_group.exception() on a cancelled future raises CancelledError or InvalidStateError. Because this is inside finally, an unexpected raise here masks the original failure and prevents ws.close() from running cleanly. Guard with a .done()/.cancelled() check or wrap in try/except.

issues.description: No tests added for 417 lines of WebSocket streaming, reconnect, and state-machine code
issues.detail: A new streaming class with reconnect logic, VAD config, and message-type dispatch lands with zero automated coverage; 'Deepgram did it without tests' is not a sufficient bar. Add a minimal mocked-websocket unit test that exercises _process_stream_event for each message_type, or repair make_test_speech. Otherwise the next refactor silently breaks this.

issues.description: Documented VAD/duration parameter ranges are never validated at construction
issues.detail: The docstring promises vad_silence_threshold_secs in [0.3, 3.0], vad_threshold in [0.1, 0.9], and duration fields in [50, 2000], but no precondition is checked. Out-of-range values reach the server and produce an opaque WS handshake failure. Enforce the ranges in __init__ so the failure mode is local and obvious.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch follows the established Deepgram/Cartesia STTv2 pattern competently and is the right shape, but needs work before landing. Highest-confidence consensus items: the audio_format cast lies to the type system and must validate sample_rate against the Literal set, the speaking-state machine duplicates dispatch logic and conflates segment-end signals (extract a single transition function), and the URL is assembled by hand instead of via urlencode. Torvalds additionally flags a latent bug in the reconnect/finally block where tasks_group.exception() on a cancelled gather can mask real errors, plus the absence of any tests for 417 lines of WebSocket/state-machine code. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — fix the correctness items, add at least a mocked unit test for _process_stream_event, then resubmit.
